scope: Focused source review of synchronous owned service ReadLease and OwnedMappedImageCaller; no console/game access
recommendation: Accept for explicit already-owned synchronous mapped-image leaf use under documented caller contract
reasoning: ReadLease acquires the authoritative service mutex before checking registry extents/permissions and retains it through all Rust borrowed reads. Checked service write/protect/free/revoke share that mutex.

Each requested range is checked, sorted and nonoverlapping; coverage traverses only actual registered entries and clips uniform protection spans to the caller-supplied end. No gap or unknown region becomes a slice.
Registration owners remain retained under lock; removal and unmap wait. Borrowed ScopedRegion still requires its original synchronous storage/external-change prohibition.

ReadLease Impl field destruction releases the mutex before span storage. Constructor failure destroys lock before member storage and permits later calls; same-thread destruction is enforced before unlock.

OwnedMappedImageCaller declares context and ranges before lease and geometry wrapper. The copied snapshot owner survives geometry wrapper destruction/constructor unwind and outlives lease unlock, preventing reentrant final owner destruction under service lock.

Permission conversion uses genuine registry flags, not user hints. Geometry checks exact snapshot readable-range coverage, including splits; code/data/slot helpers inspect only frozen descriptor spans and checked bounds.

Existing host ASan/UBSan controls demonstrate real blocked protect/free/write, rejected unknown/unreadable/gap/overlap extents and uniform page splits; caller controls and native SDK compilation receipts have exit0.
integration_conditions: Use on the constructing thread synchronously; borrowed C view must not escape caller lifetime.
No owned-memory service operation, callback that invokes that service, or potentially reentrant logging occurs before caller destruction; the lock is nonrecursive.
Caller must prevent direct writes and external permission/unmap changes outside this service. The lease cannot synchronize those.
Admission is range/permission/role checking only; no engine identity, semantic resolver correctness or runtime ABI guarantee.
